title: Huelva 2026 Awards: After Elena, Alfredo Castro and Lucía Puenzo Lead Winners
excerpt:
Chilean feature After Elena claimed the Golden Columbus at Huelva's 2026 festival.
Alfredo Castro, Lucía Puenzo and the filmmakers behind La Bola Negra also won major honors.
body_md:
Spain's Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival has announced its 2026 winners, highlighting a diverse selection of films from Latin America and Spain. The awards reflect the festival's interest in stories that blend familiar genres with social questions, intimate relationships and unexpected perspectives. This year's recognized works range from a family comedy about grief to a female-led crime story and a musical drama about Black identity and joy.

The night's highest honor, the Golden Columbus for Best Feature, went to Chilean filmmaker Shawn Garry's After Elena. Its lead actor, Alfredo Castro, also received the Best Actor prize. The film follows Roberto, a 70-year-old widower whose children move into his home after their mother Elena dies. They ostensibly want to care for him, but the prospect of their mother's inheritance complicates their motives. The film combines the emotional weight of bereavement with sharp observations about family behavior.

Castro, frequently associated with heightened and intense performances, takes a comparatively restrained, realistic approach to the role. After Elena previously premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival. Recognition at Huelva offers another opportunity for a Chilean production to reach audiences beyond its home market, particularly given the limited international coverage many Latin American films receive.

Argentine director Lucía Puenzo earned Best Director for Pepita, the Gunslinger. Known for XXY and television work including La Jauría and Señorita 89, Puenzo again brings questions of gender and power into a thriller framework. The film is based on Margarita Di Tullio, who responded to the killings of fellow sex workers in 1980s Mar del Plata by building her own brothel and nightlife business network while confronting corruption. Luisana Lopilato portrays the central figure.

Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, the Spanish filmmaking duo known as Los Javis, won Best Spanish Direction for La Bola Negra in the festival's Acento Cine Español section. The honor follows the film's Audience Award at San Sebastián and adds to a strong domestic run. The festival coverage also notes its exceptional Spanish box-office performance through November 22, 2026.

Brazilian actor Duda Santos was named Best Actress for Aly Muritiba's Funk. She plays MC Sabrina, a singer whose confident, sexually frank stage persona conceals vulnerabilities that emerge during her pursuit of success. The Special Jury Prize went to Sharon Kleinberg's I Am Mario, about a 40-year-old transgender taxi driver whose unexpected pregnancy fulfills a desire for fatherhood while challenging his understanding of masculinity.

The audience prize went to Allan Deberton's Gugu's World, Brazil's submission for the International Feature Oscar race. Rubén Ochandiano received Best Supporting Actor for Life Is, while Elías Pérez won the Andalusian directing honor for Plus Ultra. Paulina García was recognized with the City of Huelva honorary award. Taken together, the results underscore the range of filmmaking supported by Huelva rather than establishing any definitive prediction for the upcoming awards season.
seo_title: Huelva 2026 Winners: After Elena Takes Top Prize
seo_description: After Elena wins Huelva's Golden Columbus, while Alfredo Castro, Lucía Puenzo and La Bola Negra's filmmakers earn major festival honors.
